related_resources.reason: Explains the unique surviving Sasanian legal compilation, its seventh-century compilation, its case-based rather than codified character, the manuscript transmission, and the status of later editorial title.
Reconstructs estate forms and differentiated inheritance rights from cases; lawbook is selective and does not describe all households or everyday enforcement.
Discusses judges, appeals, priestly authority, social status, marriage categories and limitations of surviving legal texts; norms cannot be taken as comprehensive lived practice.
